items.name: Neurosymbolic & program synthesis
items.description: Since 1971 · 2 seed terms

sections.What the lane is: Instead of predicting the next word, write a program that solves the problem, and check it. The lane mixes old program-synthesis ideas with neural nets, and it is where François Chollet's ARC puzzles keep asking whether models can handle genuinely new tasks.

items.name: Scaling & pretraining
items.description: Since 2017 · 9 seed terms

sections.What the lane is: The discovery that bigger models, trained on more data with more compute, get predictably better, following 'scaling laws'. It turned AI into an industrial race for chips, data centres and power, and it is the idea Sutskever now says has run its course as the main engine: 'more companies than ideas'.
sections.Where it seems to be heading (Sep 2026): Still absorbing most capital (multi-gigawatt data centres), but returns from pretraining alone are debated. Scaling has shifted towards RL and inference-time compute.
sections.People the genealogy names: Jared Kaplan, Dario Amodei, Ilya Sutskever, Alec Radford, Rich Sutton (Bitter Lesson).

items.name: Alignment & safety
items.description: Since 1960 · 24 seed terms

sections.What the lane is: How do you make powerful AI do what we actually want, and know that it does? The lane runs from early warnings (Wiener, Good) through MIRI's theory to today's techniques: human-feedback training, constitutions, interpretability (looking inside the network), chain-of-thought monitoring and 'control' protocols that assume the model might be misaligned.
sections.Where it seems to be heading (Sep 2026): Growing, but still a thin stream next to capabilities (ETO, 2025). In July 2025 researchers from several rival labs argued together for keeping models' reasoning readable, so that it can be monitored (Korbak et al., 2025). The lab's notes also say that labs moved further in 2026; no source is attached to that yet, so it is left out here.

sections.What the lane is: Evolution didn't optimise one score; it kept inventing new problems and solutions. items.name: Brain-inspired learning, continual learning & generalization
items.description: Since 1949 · 4 seed terms

sections.What the lane is: Humans learn from a handful of examples, keep learning on the job, and don't forget old skills. Today's models do none of that well. This lane asks what the brain knows that current AI doesn't. It is where Sutskever places SSI's bet: generalization, continual learning, and emotions as a robust 'value function'.
sections.Where it seems to be heading (Sep 2026): Sutskever (Nov 2025): 'These models somehow just generalize dramatically worse than people.' Continual learning became a headline research goal in 2025-26, from Google's Nested Learning to SSI.
